title: Synthetic Imagination II: An exploration of composition
gist: SFI's second Synthetic Imagination symposium (September 2026) focused on composition across music, theater, cuisine, puzzles and film, probing whether imagination distinguishes humans from AI and how much a creator's human-or-machine status matters to audiences. Largely an event recap with exploratory rather than empirical claims.

themes.theme: Human imagination vs. AI as a distinguishing faculty

insights.claim: Santa Fe Institute's Synthetic Imagination organizers proposed that imagination may be the faculty that most distinguishes humans from so-called alien intelligences, including AI.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Frames 'imagination' as the residual human moat; watch whether creative-AI adoption erodes or reinforces premiums on human-made work.
insights.quote: the imagination may be the faculty that most distinguishes humans from so-called alien intelligences (AI included)
insights.locator: During last year’s event, the organizers

insights.claim: SFI framed the question of where to draw the line between human synthesis, editorializing and judgment and 'synthetic' operators performing the same tasks as more pressing in 2026 because of recent advances in AI technologies.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Signals that elite research institutions see AI capability gains as directly challenging human creative/judgment roles.
insights.quote: given the advances we have seen among AI technologies
insights.locator: During last year’s event, the organizers

insights.claim: A central open question at the SFI symposium was how much a creator's ontological status (living, dead, human or machine) matters to an audience's reception of a work.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Audience indifference to provenance would weaken the 'human-made' premium in content markets; provenance-labeling demand hinges on this.
insights.quote: how much the ontological status — that is, living, dead, human, machine — matters to an audience
insights.locator: During last year’s event, the organizers

insights.claim: David Cope's Experiments in Musical Intelligence (EMI) was an early algorithmic system that generated music in the style of different historical composers, the subject of the documentary Opus Cope: An Algorithmic Opera.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Generative style-imitation predates modern AI music; useful historical anchor for copyright/style-mimicry debates.
insights.quote: EMI was an early algorithmic system that generated music in the style of different historical composers.

insights.claim: Documentary maker Jae Shim discussed the gray areas between the fruits of human creativity and those of artificial intelligence at the closing public screening.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Blurring human/AI authorship lines remains a live cultural and legal fault line.
insights.quote: the gray areas between the fruits of human creativity and those of artificial intelligence

insights.claim: Matthew Libby's play Sisters, winner of the 2022 Neukom Institute Literary Arts Award, depicts a lifelong relationship between a young woman and her AI sibling and was staged as a reading at the SFI symposium.
insights.speaker: Santa Fe Institute
insights.so_what: Cultural normalization of AI companionship narratives foreshadows consumer acceptance of AI-relationship products.
insights.locator: On day two, playwright Matthew Libby

insights.claim: Moderator Canton Becker argued the symposium recovered the original meaning of synthesis, bringing disparate elements together into a new whole, by curating neuroscience, music, cuisine, AI, puzzles, theater and film into a single conversation.
insights.speaker: Canton Becker
insights.so_what: Cross-domain synthesis is positioned as distinctively human value-add in an AI era.
insights.quote: to bring disparate elements together into a new whole

insights.claim: Caitlin McShea characterized artistic composition as each artist striving to communicate a place in the world through a specific compositional choice, from a pentomino to a chord emphasis to a mushroom mousse.
insights.speaker: Caitlin McShea
insights.so_what: Emphasizes deliberate choice/judgment as the core of creative work, the element AI tools are contested on.
insights.quote: Each artist strives to communicate a place in this world with some compositional choice
insights.locator: Remarking on the meeting after it concluded
